question_text: A jacket sold for P1,800 after a 10% discount. What was its original price?

hint_ladder.title: Hanapin ang 100%
hint_ladder.text: Isipin mo na ang sale price ay 90% ng original. Kaya ang hinahanap mo ay yung buong 100%.

hint_ladder.title: Gamitin ang formula
hint_ladder.text: Kapag may discount, huwag mag-add; gamitin ang division. Dito: Original = 1800 ÷ 0.90.

hint_ladder.title: Simple division
hint_ladder.text: 1800 ÷ 0.90 = 2000. O kaya, i-multiply mo ang 1800 sa 10, tapos i-divide sa 9.

hint_ladder.title: I-verify mo
hint_ladder.text: Bumalik: 2000 × 0.10 = 200, kaya 2000 - 200 = 1800. P2,000 ang tamang original price.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you added 10% of the sale price instead of using the original as base. Remember: discount is on original,...

B.text: You might have chosen B because of a quick mental guess. Avoid estimating—set up the equation to avoid arithmetic slips.

C.text: Correct. You knew that P1,800 is 90% of original, so dividing by 0.90 gives P2,000.

D.text: You might have chosen D by incorrectly adding more than 10% or using the wrong base. Always divide by the paid percentage (0.90).

next_time_rule: Kapag may 'after discount,' tandaan: Final price = Paid % of original. To find original, divide final price by that % (e.g., 0.90). Wag mag-add!
deconstruct_text:
Picture this: Tita Beng sells a jacket sa kanyang ukay-ukay stall sa palengke. 10% off, kaya P1,800 na lang. Pero magkano ba talaga dapat ang original price para hindi siya lugi?

Ang formula ay simple: Original Price = Sale Price ÷ (1 - Discount Rate). Kasi ang P1,800 ay 90% na lang ng original. Ibig sabihin: 0.90 × Original = 1,800.

Para makuha ang original: i-divide ang 1,800 sa 0.90. Pwedeng gawing: 1,800 ÷ 0.90 = 1,800 × (10/9) = 2,000. Kaya P2,000 ang sagot.
